note.note:
History:
- 35-year-old male (Patrick Smith) presents with severe, intermittent frontal headaches, primarily during work hours while at his computer or in meetings; headaches started after changing jobs.
- Associated symptoms: reduced appetite, unintentional 5-pound weight loss (not noticed by others), occasional nausea with headache, tingling (described as “quick picking”) in both hands (first episode, not legs), palpitations (heart beating fast) mainly in the morning or in the elevator (~once daily), occasional shortness of breath at rest (not during exercise), and recent loss of libido (onset coincides with new job).
- Denies previous history of similar headaches or neurologic symptoms. 
- Reports elevated workplace stress (self-rated 7–8/10).
- No prior comments from others regarding weight loss or loosening clothing.
- No recreational drug use or smoking. Drinks alcohol socially (once a week, a couple of glasses of wine).

Past Medical History:
- Hyperthyroidism.
- Medications: Thyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented), taken regularly.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- No other chronic illnesses or previous hospitalizations documented.

Physical Examination:
- Not recorded (teleconsultation).
- No examination findings available.
- No mention of throat swelling, mental status changes, or focal neurologic deficits.
- No exercise-induced shortness of breath.

Impression:
- Clinical impression: Exacerbation of symptoms in a patient with hyperthyroidism on thyroxine, temporally associated with increased workplace stress and recent job change.
- Differential diagnoses, consistent with transcript and supported by DDx:
    - Hyperthyroidism or over-replacement with thyroxine: Symptoms of palpitations, weight loss, feeling hot, headaches, reduced appetite, and libido changes are suggestive in context of medical history.
    - Chronic stress/anxiety: Symptoms onset with increased job stress; somatic and autonomic complaints typical.
    - Migraine: Intermittent severe headaches (frontal, work-associated), some nausea, and tingling in hands could represent migrainous features.

Management Plan:
- Advise in-person clinic appointment for physical examination, specifically to assess cardiovascular and respiratory status.
- Arrange blood tests, including thyroid function tests, to assess adequacy of thyroxine replacement.
- Withhold additional medication until in-person assessment complete.
- Document findings and inform clinic colleagues for continuity.

Patient Summary:
- 35-year-old male with history of hyperthyroidism on thyroxine presents with new headaches, palpitations, weight loss, appetite decrease, tingling in hands, and libido loss, all of which began after starting a new, high-stress job. Main concerns include underlying thyroid dysfunction versus stress-related somatization. He will attend for in-person review with examination and thyroid bloods planned.

Key Takeaways:
- Attend the clinic for a thorough physical examination and blood tests.
- Withhold starting any new medications until after assessment.
- Use the clinic app to book the next available appointment; all current information will be relayed to attending providers.

Next Steps:
- Book in-person clinic appointment for exam and testing.
- Obtain thyroid function tests.
- Follow-up plan to be determined pending results and clinical examination.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Vitals, full physical exam, mental health screening, and medication dose/route/frequency not captured. Family medical history not discussed.
● No conflicts detected between transcript and DDx.
● Transcript is clear and complete for the history; as expected for teleconsultation, no physical findings or labs are available.
